Defining hair loss, keratoderma, nail dystrophy and premature tooth loss from caries; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Congenital retinal dystrophy; supplied HPO reports seizures and structural brain abnormalities at 30-79%, supporting neurologic involvement with subtype variability.
Adrenal aldosterone excess, hypokalemia and early severe hypertension define disease; ventricular hypertrophy and cerebral hemorrhage are occasional.
Inherited ichthyosis with marked cutaneous hyperkeratosis; no common extracutaneous damage established across subtypes.
Menstrual pain without underlying pelvic pathology; purely reproductive condition.
Brain/developmental and skeletal malformations; cleft palate and strabismus each 30-79%; nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immune damage.
Vascular malformations, limb overgrowth and cutaneous capillary lesions define syndrome; GI vascular bleeding reported at 30-79%; embolism/cellulitis are separate complications.
Carcinoma originates in maxillary sinus mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Immune-mediated necrotizing vasculitis; renal injury occurs in roughly 70-90% and respiratory tract inflammation in roughly 40-80% across major subtypes.
Congenital underdevelopment of internal carotid arteries; cerebral infarction is not established as common or defining.
Cranial nerve neuralgia involving facial or trigeminal neural pathways; facial pain does not establish damage to other organs.
Malignancy of the hepatopancreatic ampulla, spanning the terminal biliary channel and its duodenal junction.
Central autonomic failure causes hypoventilation without intrinsic lung disease; Hirschsprung disease (~16-30%) is separately diagnosed; reduced heart-rate variability is neural.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize the deletion spectrum; cardiac and hematologic defects depend on the deleted interval and are not established across the umbrella.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; extranodal disease varies, with no additional organ established as involved in at least 30%.
Childhood neoplasm located in the cerebellum.
Hereditary prostate malignancy; prostate is reproductive, with no defining endocrine dysfunction or common direct damage to another axis.
Vascular neoplasm of splenic red-pulp sinus lining; spleen and vascular origin define disease. Immunological associations do not establish an immune mechanism.
Small cell carcinoma arising in salivary glands; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine organ disease.
SYCP3-related failure of spermatogenesis causing azoospermia and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine disease.
Malignancy located in short bones of the lower limb.
Umbrella for pathological processes of the colon; no additional organ or mechanism applies across the group.
FBXO7-related parkinsonian and pyramidal degeneration; fixed talipes reported in 10/10 supports skeletal involvement. Dysphagia and neurogenic bladder reflect neural dysfunction.
Congenital duplication of small-intestinal structures, including duodenal and jejunoileal forms.
